subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Which parts of this multi-agent collaboration stack should OpenClaw core own, and which should be narrowed into plugins, ClawHub packages, or existing related RFCs?
rationale: The request conflicts with lean-core and heavy-orchestration guardrails while also touching security and memory boundaries; automation cannot choose the permanent product boundary or trust model.

options.title: Keep umbrella, split accepted slices
options.body: Keep this issue open as the broad RFC and ask maintainers to split only approved core/API work into narrower issues such as budget enforcement, capability routing, or blackboard access-control design.

options.title: Move most work out of core
options.body: Use current plugin and ClawHub boundaries for optional coordination layers, keeping core work limited to missing extension APIs and security primitives.

options.title: Defer as not planned
options.body: Close or freeze the RFC if maintainers decide heavy multi-agent orchestration should not be part of OpenClaw's near-term direction.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella, split accepted slices
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the broad RFC and ask maintainers to split only approved core/API work into narrower issues such as budget enforcement, capability routing, or blackboard access-control design.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily product architecture and lean-core scope, and steipete has adjacent subagent cleanup history plus likely ownership of broad project direction.
